title: Infra: GPU fleet, cloud accounts & IaC CI/CD consolidated playbook (2026)
author: Evelyn Chen
content:
Summary:
This consolidated playbook captures engineering standards, ownership, and runbooks for the GPU fleet and capacity planning, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC module patterns, and CI/CD build pipelines used by Redwood Inference (2026 baseline). It is intended as the canonical operational reference for infra engineers, oncall SREs, and platform feature owners.

Goals and scope:
- Provide a single reference that links capacity rules, network/account boundaries, IaC patterns, and build/runbook steps.
- Cover normal ops (scale/balance), incident response (capacity/network outages), and planned changes (cluster upgrades, module releases).
- Audience: infra engineers, platform engineers, SRE, release engineers, and solutions engineers supporting Dedicated/Private customers.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Fleet owner: infra-gpu-team (primary), infra-networking-team (networking), eng-sre (oncall).
- Service names: gpu-proxy, gpu-scheduler, kv-cache-store, inference-agent, private-deploy-controlplane.
- Target SLOs: cluster-level uptime 99.95% (monthly), median p95 request queuing latency < 20ms, autoscaler reaction time (scale-up) < 2 minutes for reactive bursts.
- Capacity buffer policy: maintain a 20% reserved headroom on committed pools for Dedicated; 10% for hosted regions.

1) GPU fleet & capacity planning
Overview:
- Fleet composition: a mix of instance families optimized for different workloads (A100 80GB, H100, L40s) and quantized/CPU fallbacks for cheaper tiers. Pools are labeled by accelerator, memory, and capability (e.g., "gpu-a100-80g-highmem", "gpu-h100-lowlatency").

Capacity tiers and targets:
- Baseline commit pools: reserved capacity for Dedicated customers (monthly commit). Maintain 2h cold-start provisioning SLA for non-burst nodes.
- Burst pools: on-demand capacity used for spikes; autoscaler target occupancy < 85% during business hours.
- Spot/Preemptible fallback: used for non-critical batch workloads; pipelines must support graceful eviction.

Forecasting process (monthly):
1. Collect usage by pool (tokens/sec, median sequence length, p95 concurrency) from cost/metrics dashboard.
2. Run model-specific unit economics (tokens per GPU-hour) and update quantization recommendations.
3. Propose capacity changes and publish PR to capacity-tracking board two weeks before planned change.

Runbook: scale-up procedure (planned)
1. Create capacity request PR in infra-capacity repo with: pool name, instance type, desired nodes, expected go-live date, owner, rollback plan.
2. Run CI checks: terraform plan, static checks, cost estimate.
3. Approve with capacity leads and SRE.
4. Apply during maintenance window; monitor autoscaler events and request latencies for 60 minutes.
5. Rollback if request latency increases >20% or error rates rise above 0.5% for requests to gpu-proxy.

2) Cloud accounts & networking (multi-account strategy)
Account model:
- Root org: management account with centralized logging/Audit (CloudTrail), billing, and organization guardrails.
- Workload accounts: per-region workload accounts grouped by environment (prod-us, prod-eu, staging, private-customer-<id>).
- Shared services account: networking, NAT gateways, transit routing, and DNS zones.

Networking patterns:
- VPC-per-account with centralized transit/virtual-router in shared services. Use AWS Transit Gateway (or cloud equivalent) with enforced route tables for cross-account traffic.
- Default CIDR planning: avoid overlapping /16 blocks; allocate per-region /12 namespace from company allocation.
- Security groups: least privilege for infra services; egress-only for worker nodes except to KMS and telemetry endpoints.

Cross-account private connectivity for Private deployments:
- Use VPC peering or managed private-link endpoints for control plane connectivity. All private endpoints require mutual TLS and customer-provided CIDR allowances.
- Enforce ingress ACLs at transit layer and apply per-customer Egress policies.

Network runbook: troubleshooting high latency between control plane and GPU pool
1. Verify CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics for packet drops and retransmits on the ENI.
2. Check Transit Gateway route table consistency and NACLs for recent changes.
3. Validate NATgateway/IGW health if egress flows are failing.
4. If packet loss persists, perform host-level tcpdump and open an incident with infra-networking-team.

3) Terraform / IaC module standards
Principles:
- Modules must be opinionated, composable, and publishable. Keep variable count minimal and expose only consumer-level knobs.
- Enforce tagging, cost-center, owner, and environment tags on every resource.
- State: use remote state with locking (DynamoDB/Cloud KMS). State per-environment and per-service.

Module layout (recommended):
- modules/
  - vpc/
  - gpu-node-pool/
  - autoscaler/
  - iam/
  - datadog-monitoring/
  - cloudwatch-logging/

Release process:
1. Bump module version and create release branch.
2. Run module integration tests in a disposable account (smoke create/destroy).
3. Publish registry entry and update dependent stacks via automated PRs.

Example module usage (snippet):
```
module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwood.ai/infra/modules/gpu-node-pool.git//v1.4"
  name   = "gpu-h100-lowlatency-prod"
  instance_type = "h100.80x"
  desired_capacity = 40
  min_capacity = 10
  max_capacity = 200
  tags = {
    owner = "infra-gpu-team"
    env   = "prod-us"
  }
}
```

4) CI/CD and build pipeline standards
Pipeline roles:
- IaC pipeline: terraform fmt/validate, terratest/integration jobs, plan preview, manual approval gate for prod apply.
- Image build pipeline: base images (gpu-optimized CUDA/runtime), inference-agent images signed and pushed to private registry.
- Release pipeline: module release -> stack PR -> canary rollout -> full rollout.

Key checks and gates:
- Prevent prod apply without: signed changelog, capacity owner approval, cost estimate < threshold (auto block otherwise).
- Automated smoke test post-deploy: create a short inference request and assert p95 latency within expected SLA.

Example CI steps (Terraform stack):
1. Checkout and run "terraform init" (use backend configuration selector).
2. Run "terraform fmt" and "terraform validate".
3. Run plan and publish plan artefact.
4. Merge triggers build job for non-prod and a manual "prod-apply" job for prod.

5) Runbooks and oncall procedures
Incident triage playbook (GPU capacity saturation)
1. Pager triggers to infra-gpu-oncall. Acknowledge within 5 minutes.
2. Check cluster occupancy and pending pods. If pending > 5% of running, and autoscaler not scaling, follow autoscaler runbook.
3. If autoscaler healthy but nodes at 100% utilization, enact emergency scale: temporarily increase pool max by 30% via emergency-config repo and apply.
4. Notify product/customer-impact channel and start mitigation timeline (target less than 30 minutes to add capacity).
5. After stabilization, open postmortem and adjust forecasting/thresholds if needed.

Escalation matrix:
- infra-gpu-oncall -> infra-sre -> infra-platform-eng -> VP infra (if > 4 hours unresolved or customer SLA breach).

Post-deploy checklist (for major upgrades):
- Verify autoscaler metrics and test traffic through canary hosts.
- Run end-to-end inference smoke tests (2 models, short/long sequences).
- Confirm roll-forward/rollback playbooks and snapshot states.

6) Knowledge base and team wiki usage
- Keep this playbook current: property owners must review quarterly and after any major fleet topology change.
- Use the following labels on change PRs: [gpu-change], [network-impact], [iac-release].
- Store runbooks in runbooks/ and link to this consolidated page for cross-reference.

Appendices
A. Capacity thresholds (summary table)
- Pool occupancy target: 60-75% (sustained).
- Autoscaler spike threshold: 85% sustained for 60s.
- Emergency scale trigger: pending requests > 5% OR median queueing latency > 100ms for 5 minutes.

B. Quick commands
- Terraform plan preview: `make infra-plan STACK=prod-us`
- Apply non-prod: `make infra-apply STACK=staging`
- Run a canary inference test: `scripts/canary-test --model gpt-redwood-7b --seq 512 --qps 5`

C. Links (internal)
- Capacity board: /boards/infra-capacity
- IaC modules registry: /registry/infra-modules
- GPU metrics dashboard: /dashboards/gpu-fleet-overview

Contact and feedback:
- Page owner: Evelyn Chen (infra-gpu-team). For corrections or updates open a PR on the infra-wiki repo and tag reviewers listed above.

Document history:

- 2026-03-04: updated capacity thresholds, added H100 pool guidance and CI/CD gating rules.
